newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lion Nathan rejects discounting talk.
newsitem.headline: Lion Nathan rejects discounting talk.

text.p: Lion Nathan Ltd unit Lion Breweries on Thursday rejected talk that it was selling cheap beer to improve its market share, the New Zealand Press Association reported.
DB Group Managing director Erik Korthals Altes said on Wednesday that Lion was trying to start a beer price war and DB would not buy into it.
Korthals Altes said Lion was discounting major brands such as Lion Red and Ice to levels below their value to regain lost market share.
Lion Breweries Central managing director Iain Abercrombie said it was DB which was staging a price war. He said DB was discounting its weaker draught brands to try to gain market share.

He acknowledged Lion had been through a major restructure in the past six months with some of its middle managers being made redundant but said some of them had been replaced by people with good experience in the liquor industry.
Abercrombie said because of the restructure, DB could perceive "Lion as in a state of turmoil".
"That is not the case, the restructure has been done for sound business reasons. The business has been streamlined; it is very competitive market which is declining."
The only area that was not declining was the premium beer (Heineken and Steinlager) market. It has been growing at about 10 percent a year off a low base.
Lion Ice had been discounted from time to time but Abercrombie said it was not a premium brand.
"We see it as being a mainstream-plus brand."
In the central region DB has a larger market share than Lion. But in the South Island and the top of the North Island, Lion has the larger share.
DB shares were up one cent at NZ$1.03 this morning and Lion shares were down six at $3.59.
